topics.legal_basis: Mehr in Pakistan is legally recognized under Section 10 of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance (MFLO), 1961. A wife can demand her mehr at any point during the marriage, and the husband is legally obligated to pay it. Mehr is recorded in the Nikahnama at the time of marriage, and courts recognize a wife's right to it even where the Nikahnama is incomplete. Mehr belongs entirely to the wife as her personal property and can be claimed even after divorce.
topics.islamic_basis: Surah An-Nisa, verse 4, instructs husbands to give women their mehr willingly, as an obligation. In his commentary Tafheem-ul-Quran, Maulana Abul Ala Maududi explains this verse as establishing mehr as a duty owed directly to the wife, not to her guardians or family. The verse also affirms that a wife may, entirely of her own free will, choose to give up part of her mehr.
sources: Tafheem-ul-Quran, Surah An-Nisa 4:4, commentary by Maulana Abul Ala Maududi: https://www.islamicstudies.info/tafheem.php?sura=4&verse=4&to=4
Quran Gallery - analysis of Surah An-Nisa 4:4 on mahr as a wife's exclusive right: https://qurangallery.app/by-ayah/mahr-meaning-surah-an-nisa-4-4-bridal-gift

qa.question: Mera mehr ada nahi hua, kya main abhi bhi le sakti hoon?
qa.answer: Haan. Mehr aapka qanooni haq hai jo Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 ke tehat protect hai. Aap shaadi ke doran ya baad mein bhi mehr ka mutalba kar sakti hain, chahe talaq ho chuki ho. Behtar hoga ke apne Nikahnama ki copy nikalwayein aur zaroorat parne par Union Council ya family lawyer se raabta karein.

qa.question: Kya sasural wale mera mehr rok saktay hain?
qa.answer: Nahin. Mehr sirf aapki milkiyat hai - na shohar, na sasural wale isay rok saktay hain. Quran mein Surah An-Nisa ki ayat 4 mein saaf kaha gaya hai ke mehr seedha biwi ko diya jaye, na ke uske sarparaston ko. Yeh aapka qanooni aur deeni dono lehaz se haq hai.

qa.question: Nikahnama mein mehr ki raqam likhi nahi gayi, kya phir bhi haq hai?
qa.answer: Haan, mehr ka haq khatam nahi hota chahe Nikahnama mein raqam waazeh na likhi ho. Aap apne family lawyer ya Union Council se rehnumai le sakti hain ke is soorat mein mehr ka tayin kaise hoga.

qa.question: Kya mein apna mehr maaf kar sakti hoon?
qa.answer: Haan, lekin yeh sirf aapki apni marzi se hona chahiye, kisi dabao ya majboori mein nahi. Quran isay khud biwi ka ikhtiyar batata hai - koi aur yeh faisla aapki taraf se nahi kar sakta.

qa.question: Talaq ke baad mehr ka kya hota hai?
qa.answer: Mehr talaq se khatam nahi hota. Agar mehr pehle se ada nahi hua tha, to talaq ke baad bhi aap iska mutalba kar sakti hain.

qa.question: Kya mehr sirf paison ki shakal mein hota hai?
qa.answer: Nahin, mehr paisa, zewar, jaidad ya koi bhi qeemti cheez ho sakti hai jo Nikah ke waqt tay ki gayi ho. Jo bhi tay hua ho, woh aapka haq hai.

topics.legal_basis: Maintenance rights are covered under Section 9 of the MFLO 1961. A husband is legally responsible for financially maintaining his wife and children. If he fails to provide maintenance, the wife can approach the Union Council/Chairman, which can refer the matter to an Arbitration Council to enforce payment. If the Union Council's decision isn't satisfactory, there is a further right of revision before the Collector.
topics.islamic_basis: Surah An-Nisa, verse 34, describes men as qawwamun. Maulana Maududi's Tafheem-ul-Quran explains this as someone responsible for the right conduct, safeguard, and maintenance of the affairs of the family, tied specifically to the fact that men spend of their wealth to support their wives. This financial responsibility is the basis of the guardian role, not a license for control. Dr. Israr Ahmed's lecture similarly clarifies this role does not grant permission to neglect or oppress a wife's rights.
topics.unresolved_nuance_flagged_for_scholar_re: Whether a man who does not provide maintenance is still considered 'qawwam' is debated among scholars. Hanafi view: the marriage/role isn't automatically voided, but maintenance remains an enforceable debt. Maliki/Shafi'i view: inability to provide can be grounds for dissolution. This should not be answered definitively by the chatbot - route to Tier 2/3 escalation if asked directly.
sources: Tafheem-ul-Quran, Surah An-Nisa 4:34, commentary by Maulana Abul Ala Maududi: https://quranx.com/tafsirs/4.34

Dr. Israr Ahmed - lecture on qawwamun, financial provision, and rights of women within marriage: https://www.drisrar.com/watch/husband-or-wife-who-is-head-of-family-allah-s-verdict-dr-israr-ahmed_V01065.html

qa.question: Mera shohar mujhe kharcha nahi deta, mein kya karoon?
qa.answer: Nafaqa (kharcha) dena shohar ki qanooni zimmedari hai, jo Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961 ke Section 9 mein darj hai. Agar shohar ada nahi kar raha, aap apne ilaqe ke Union Council mein darkhwast de sakti hain, jahan Arbitration Council maamla dekhegi. Agar wahan se insaaf na mile, aap Collector ke paas revision ke liye ja sakti hain.

qa.question: Kya talaq ke baad bhi nafaqa mil sakta hai?
qa.answer: Iddat ke doran nafaqa ka haq mojood hota hai. Har case mukhtalif ho sakta hai, is liye apne mahol ke mutabiq kisi family lawyer ya Union Council se mashwara zaroor karein.

qa.question: Islam mein shohar par kharche ki zimmedari kyun hai?
qa.answer: Quran, Surah An-Nisa ayat 34 mein, mardon ko "qawwam" kaha gaya hai - yani woh jo apne maal se apni family ka kharcha uthata hai aur unki hifazat karta hai. Yeh zimmedari aurat ko dabane ke liye nahi, balke uski dekhbhal aur tahafuz ke liye di gayi hai.

qa.question: Agar shohar kaam nahi karta ya kharcha dene se inkaar kare, to kya yeh Islami taleemat ke khilaf hai?
qa.answer: Haan, nafaqa dena shohar par farz hai. Agar woh jaan boojh kar apni zimmedari se inkaar kare, yeh uski deeni zimmedari se hatna hai. Aap qanooni raasta (Union Council, Arbitration Council) istemal kar sakti hain apna haq lene ke liye.

qa.question: Kya sirf khana aur kapda hi nafaqa hai, ya aur bhi cheezein shamil hain?
qa.answer: Nafaqa mein rehaish, khana, kapda, aur zaroori zindagi ke kharche shamil hain. Yeh mahol aur waqt ke mutabiq tay hota hai - jo us ilaqe mein munasib samjha jaye.

qa.question: Kya sasural walon ka kharcha bhi shohar par farz hai, ya sirf biwi ka?
qa.answer: Shohar ki bunyadi zimmedari apni biwi aur bachon ka kharcha uthana hai. Sasural walon ka kharcha alag maamla hai aur is par qanooni rai family lawyer se lena behtar hoga.

topics.legal_basis: The FIA's Cyber Crime Wing has been replaced by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), established under Section 51 of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016. National reporting helpline: 1991. For bank-specific fraud: State Bank of Pakistan consumer protection desk (cpd.helpdesk@sbp.org.pk) or Banking Mohtasib Pakistan (0800-44522), which resolves bank disputes for free. Under the SBP's Electronic Fund Transfers Regulations 2018, the burden of proof for unauthorized transfers is on the bank, not the customer.
topics.islamic_basis: Surah An-Nisa, verse 29, instructs believers not to consume one another's wealth through falsehood or deception, and only through mutually agreed, lawful transactions. This is the Quranic foundation for why scams, fraud, and exploitation of the vulnerable are considered a serious wrong, not just a legal offense.

qa.question: Mujhe kisi ne call kiya aur bola woh bank se hai, mera ATM PIN maanga, kya karoon?
qa.answer: Kabhi bhi apna ATM PIN, OTP ya password kisi ko na batayein, chahe woh khud ko bank ka numainda kahe. Asli banks kabhi phone par yeh maloomat nahi maangte. Agar shak ho, foran apne bank ko khud call karein (jo number aapke pass pehle se ho) aur is waqia ki report NCCIA helpline 1991 par karein.

qa.question: Agar mere account se paise ghalat tareeqe se nikal gaye hain, kya wapas mil saktay hain?
qa.answer: Haan, agar transfer aapki ijazat ke baghair hua hai, State Bank ke qawaid ke mutabiq bank ki zimmedari hai ke woh saabit kare ke transfer aapki marzi se hua. Foran apne bank ko inform karein, aur agar bank sahi jawab na de to Banking Mohtasib Pakistan (0800-44522) par mufta shikayat darj karwayein.

qa.question: Koi mujhe bol raha hai ke thora paisa lagayen aur double mil jayega, kya karoon?
qa.answer: Yeh aksar dhoka hota hai. Koi bhi asli sarmaya kaari (investment) itni jaldi double munafa nahi deti. Aisi offers se bachein, aur kisi bhi paisa lagane se pehle kisi bharosemand bank ya family member se mashwara zaroor karein.

qa.question: Mujhe naya SIM lene gayi thi, dukandar ne mera angootha lagaya aur bola SIM kal milega, kya yeh theek hai?
qa.answer: Yeh ek jaana pehchana dhoka hai jahan aapke angoothe ke nishan ka ghalat istemal karke doosra SIM activate kiya ja sakta hai. Sirf officially registered franchise se hi SIM lein, aur agar shak ho to PTA ko report karein.

qa.question: Mujhe WhatsApp par job ka offer mila hai jisme pehle paisa jama karwana keh rahe hain, kya yeh sahi hai?
qa.answer: Nahin, asli companies kabhi job dene se pehle paisa nahi maangti. Yeh ek aam scam hai. Aise kisi bhi offer mein paisa na bhejein aur agar shak ho to NCCIA helpline 1991 par report karein.

qa.question: Kisi ne mujhe mera CNIC number aur tasveer maang li, kya yeh dena chahiye?
qa.answer: Sirf unhi jagah apni CNIC details dein jo aap achi tarah jaanti hon aur bharosemand hon (jaise bank, sarkari daftar). Anjaan logon, calls, ya online forms ko apni CNIC details na dein - is se identity theft ho sakti hai.

sources: Surah at-Tawbah 9:60 (the eight eligible recipients of Zakat)

qa.question: What is Nisab?
qa.answer: Nisab is the minimum amount of wealth a Muslim must own before Zakat becomes obligatory. Think of it as a starting line: if your qualifying wealth is below this line, you owe no Zakat at all. If you are at or above it, Zakat becomes due on the whole qualifying amount.

qa.question: When do I have to pay Zakat? What is the one lunar year rule (Hawl)?
qa.answer: For cash, gold, silver, business stock, and livestock, your wealth must stay at or above Nisab for one full Islamic lunar year (354 days) before Zakat is due on it. Pick one fixed date each year as your personal Zakat anniversary. On that date, calculate 2.5% of everything you currently hold that qualifies, regardless of when during the year you earned each portion.

qa.question: Do crops and minerals also wait a full year before Zakat is due?
qa.answer: No. Crops do not need a waiting year - Zakat is paid right at harvest, even if you harvest more than once a year. Minerals and buried treasure are paid immediately at the moment of discovery.

qa.question: How much Zakat do I pay on my cash and gold savings?
qa.answer: This is the most common category, covering savings, cash on hand, gold, and silver. Nisab is 85g of 24K gold (about 97.1g for 21K gold), or 595g of silver, or cash equal to that value. The rate is 2.5%, paid once a year on your Zakat anniversary date.

qa.question: How does Zakat work for a business or trade goods?
qa.answer: If you run a business, Zakat applies to everything you hold for sale - inventory, raw materials, finished products, and business cash. Nisab is the market value equal to 85g gold or 595g silver. The rate is 2.5% yearly on the total wholesale value of sellable stock and business cash.

qa.question: What is Ushr and how much Zakat is paid on farm produce?
qa.answer: Zakat on farm produce is called Ushr. Unlike cash, there is no one-year wait; it is paid the day you harvest. Nisab is 5 Wasqs (roughly 653 kg / 1,440 lbs of dry grain or fruit). The rate is 10% if the land was rain or river fed with no irrigation cost, or 5% if it was artificially irrigated (water was pumped or paid for).

qa.question: How does Zakat work on livestock?
qa.answer: Zakat on livestock applies to free-grazing animals raised for their produce, like milk or breeding, not for resale. Nisab is a minimum of 5 camels, 30 cows or buffaloes, or 40 sheep or goats. The rate is a fixed number of animals owed, based on herd-size brackets. Note: livestock raised to be sold commercially is treated as a business trade asset under the 2.5% rule instead.

qa.question: What is Zakat on minerals or buried treasure (Rikaz)?
qa.answer: Minerals and buried treasure (Rikaz) cover valuable resources extracted from the earth, or ancient treasure found with no known owner. There is no Nisab - it applies to any significant find. The rate is 20% (called Khumus), paid immediately upon extraction or discovery.

qa.question: Who is eligible to receive Zakat?
qa.answer: The Quran, in Surah at-Tawbah 9:60, names exactly eight groups who may receive Zakat: the poor (severe poverty, virtually no income), the needy (earn something but not enough for basic needs), Zakat administrators (officials who collect and distribute it), those whose hearts are being reconciled (new converts or people being welcomed into the community), those freeing themselves from slavery or bondage, people with legitimate survival debts they cannot repay, those striving in the cause of Allah (religious education, community welfare, defense), and stranded travelers cut off from their money.

qa.question: What is Zakat al-Fitr and how is it different from regular Zakat?
qa.answer: Zakat al-Fitr is separate from Zakat al-Mal (wealth Zakat). It is smaller, simpler, and tied to Ramadan rather than yearly wealth. Every Muslim pays it regardless of Nisab, and a head of household pays on behalf of dependents too. It is due before the Eid al-Fitr prayer, at the end of Ramadan. The amount is about one Sa' (roughly 2.5-3 kg) of a staple food, or its cash equivalent. Its purpose is to purify the fasting person's Ramadan and to ensure the poor can also celebrate Eid.

qa.question: Can I subtract my debts before calculating Zakat?
qa.answer: Yes. Before applying the 2.5% rate, most scholars allow you to subtract debts and bills that are currently due, and essential living expenses already set aside. What is left after these deductions is your net zakatable wealth, and that is the figure compared against Nisab.

qa.question: Who is exempt from paying Zakat?
qa.answer: Anyone whose wealth is below Nisab is exempt, as is anyone whose debts are greater than their zakatable assets. Non-Muslims are not obligated to pay Zakat, though voluntary charity (Sadaqah) is encouraged for everyone.

qa.question: Do I pay Zakat on my monthly salary?
qa.answer: A monthly salary is not a separate Zakat category - it is simply treated as cash once it lands in your account, added to your total savings, with the one-year Hawl rule applied to the combined amount from your fixed Zakat anniversary date. Some scholars allow paying Zakat on each salary payment separately as it is received instead of waiting for the annual date; both approaches are considered valid, though the annual method is more common.

qa.question: Do I have to pay Zakat on stocks and shares I own?
qa.answer: It depends on why you hold the shares. If you actively trade them for short-term profit, they are treated like trade goods and Zakat is due on the full current market value at 2.5%. If you hold them long-term for dividends or growth, many scholars say you only owe Zakat on the company's underlying zakatable assets proportional to your shareholding, since much of a company's value sits in non-zakatable assets like factories or equipment. In practice this is hard to calculate precisely, so some scholars simplify it to roughly 25-30% of the share's market value, or Zakat only on dividends received.

qa.question: Do I pay Zakat on my pension or retirement fund?
qa.answer: The key question is whether you can access the money now or not. For inaccessible funds, like an employer pension you cannot touch until retirement age, most scholars say no Zakat is due yet since you don't truly own or control the wealth; it becomes due once you actually receive it. For accessible funds, like a personal investment account you could withdraw from anytime even with a penalty, it is more likely to be zakatable annually like ordinary savings.

qa.question: Do I pay Zakat on property or a house I own?
qa.answer: It depends on the property's purpose. Your own home is never zakatable, regardless of its value. For rental property you intend to keep long-term, the property itself is not zakatable, but the rental income you collect is treated as cash and included in your annual Zakat calculation after deducting expenses and debts. Property bought purely to resell for profit is treated as a trade good, so its full current market value is zakatable at 2.5% every year it remains unsold.

qa.question: Do I need to say out loud that a payment is Zakat?
qa.answer: You must internally intend that the payment is specifically Zakat and not general charity (Sadaqah). This is a condition of the heart - it does not need to be spoken aloud or declared to anyone.

qa.question: Do the different Islamic schools of thought agree on Zakat rules?
qa.answer: The four major Sunni schools (Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali) agree on the core rules of Zakat but differ on some details, such as how to calculate Nisab when cash, gold, and silver are mixed together, and whether personal-use jewelry is zakatable - the Hanafi school generally says yes, while other schools often exempt it if it stays within customary, reasonable amounts. If unsure which school's ruling applies, it is best to consult a local scholar or trusted Islamic authority.

qa.question: Does Zakat apply to women too? Do I owe Zakat on my own wealth even though I am married?
qa.answer: Yes, Zakat applies equally to women and men - it is tied purely to wealth ownership, not gender. Any Muslim adult who personally owns qualifying wealth for a full lunar year owes Zakat on it, calculated the same way. In Islamic law, a wife's income, savings, gold, property, or business assets belong solely to her and are not automatically merged with her husband's wealth. If she owns qualifying wealth, she is personally responsible for her own Zakat, separate from her husband's. A husband is not obligated to pay Zakat on his wife's wealth, and a wife is not obligated to pay on her husband's - though a husband may choose to pay it on her behalf if she asks and he agrees, the responsibility itself remains legally hers.

qa.question: Do I have to pay Zakat on my gold jewelry that I wear?
qa.answer: This is the main point of scholarly difference, and it applies mostly to women since they are the more common holders of jewelry. The Hanafi school says personal-use gold or silver jewelry is zakatable if it reaches Nisab, no matter how customary the amount is. The Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali schools generally exempt jewelry worn regularly for personal use, as long as it stays within reasonable, customary limits and isn't hoarded as an investment.

qa.question: What is Mirath (inheritance) in Islam?
qa.answer: Mirath is the gross inheritance: all movable or immovable property left behind by a deceased person, whether they earned it, inherited it, or were gifted it. It is distributed among their Warith (heirs) according to a fixed order and process.

qa.question: What is the order in which a deceased person's wealth is distributed?
qa.answer: There is a fixed sequence: first, modest funeral expenditure is paid. Second, any outstanding debts or loans are paid off. Third, any pending commitments are settled. Fourth, a will (Wassiya) of up to one-third of what remains can be carried out. Only after all of that is the remaining wealth distributed among the heirs according to their prescribed shares.

qa.question: What is a Wassiya (Islamic will) and how much of my property can I will away?
qa.answer: A Wassiya is an order for allocating a certain amount of a deceased person's property after death, based on their wishes - it only takes effect after death, not during their lifetime. A will can only cover up to one-third of the total property; if someone tries to will more than that, only the one-third portion will actually be carried out. A will cannot be made in favor of someone who is already entitled to a fixed share as an heir - it can only be used for people who do not otherwise inherit, such as an orphaned grandchild, a non-Muslim family member, an adopted or step-child, or for charity.

qa.question: Who counts as a child (Walad) for inheritance purposes?
qa.answer: For inheritance purposes, children (Walad) include: son, daughter, son's son, son's daughter, son's son's son, and son's son's daughter. Other types of grandchildren, such as through a daughter, fall into a different, lower-tier category and are treated differently.

qa.question: What are the different tiers or categories of heirs in Islamic inheritance?
qa.answer: There are three tiers. The first tier (Dhil-Furoodh) are heirs who have a prescribed, fixed proportion of the estate under different circumstances. The second tier (Asbah, or residuary) do not have a fixed proportion; after the first tier is paid, whatever remains goes to the closest relation among this group. The third tier (Dhil-Irham) only receives anything if there is leftover property and no one from the first two tiers exists; the closest relative in this category then receives all the remaining share.

qa.question: Can a daughter inherit if there is also a son?
qa.answer: Yes, a daughter is always entitled to a share of inheritance regardless of whether there is also a son. The exact proportion depends on which other relatives are alive at the time of death, and requires a proper calculation - a scholar or the full calculation method can work out the precise share for a specific family situation.

qa.question: Can I write a will for my non-Muslim relative, adopted child, or someone who wouldn't normally inherit?
qa.answer: Yes. A will (Wassiya) exists specifically for people who would not otherwise receive a share as an heir - such as an orphaned grandchild, a non-Muslim family member, an adopted child, or a step-child - or for charitable purposes. It is limited to at most one-third of the total estate, and it cannot be used to give an additional share to someone who already inherits as a fixed heir.

qa.question: Can I change my will after I've written it? When does it actually take effect?
qa.answer: A will can be changed and updated again and again during a person's lifetime, and the most recent version is the one that is used. It is only applicable and actionable after death - it has no effect while the person who made it is still alive.

qa.question: What happens if someone makes a wrong or unfair will - like leaving more than a third, or denying a rightful heir their share?
qa.answer: Making a wrong will - such as using more than one-third of the wealth, favoring an heir who is already entitled to a share, or denying a legitimate heir their due share - is considered a major sin in Islamic teaching. It should ideally be corrected during the person's lifetime; if it isn't, the heirs are encouraged to correct it themselves after the person's death.

qa.question: Can someone who caused the death of the deceased still inherit from them?
qa.answer: No. Someone who killed the deceased is disqualified from inheriting from them, even if they would otherwise have had a prescribed share. This is based on a hadith recorded in Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and Abu Dawud: 'One who kills a man cannot inherit from him.'

qa.question: Can a non-Muslim relative inherit from a Muslim, or a Muslim inherit from a non-Muslim relative?
qa.answer: No. A non-Muslim does not inherit from a Muslim, and a Muslim does not inherit from a non-Muslim, based on hadith in Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. If someone wants to leave something to a non-Muslim relative, they can use their will (up to one-third of their wealth) for that purpose, since a will can be made for people who don't otherwise inherit.

qa.question: Does a child born outside of marriage inherit from the father?
qa.answer: A child born out of wedlock is regarded, for inheritance purposes, as the child of the mother only. It's worth noting that falsely denying paternity of a child is considered a major sin in Islamic teaching. This is a sensitive area with real legal and personal implications, so it is best discussed with a scholar or lawyer for a specific situation.

qa.question: What are the practical steps to make a valid Islamic will?
qa.answer: A valid will should be written or verbal, and witnessed by two people who are trustworthy, honest, and have no conflict of interest in the inheritance or the will itself. It should also be written to satisfy the legal requirements of the country you live in, so it can actually be executed under local law - for example, some countries allow Islamic distribution to be followed if it's explicitly stated in a legally valid will; otherwise the country's default inheritance law would apply instead. It's recommended to write a will as soon as possible while in sound mind, rather than delaying it.

qa.question: I want to know exactly how much each of my family members will inherit - can you calculate it?
keywords: how much will each heir get
qa.answer: Exact inheritance shares depend on the full set of heirs alive at the time of death and require a detailed calculation method (using fixed-share tables, residuary rules, and sometimes adjustments for excess or deficiency). This chatbot can explain the general principles, but for an exact calculation for your specific family situation, it's best to consult a qualified scholar or an Islamic inheritance calculator/specialist so the numbers are accurate.
